points.description: States that a class can have an unlimited (any number of) constructors, in any wording (e.g. "as many as you want", "no limit", "any number, as long as their parameter lists differ").
points.partial_credit: Half or more of the marks for a vague or partly wrong statement, e.g. "many" or "more than one" without saying there is no limit, or an unlimited claim with a minor error.

points.description: Gives the supporting detail that the constructors are overloaded, i.e. they must differ in their parameters (number or types).

rubric.notes: Full marks for P1 if the student says unlimited, any number or no limit, in any wording; even a very brief answer earns this. Part marks for vague answers such as "many" or "more than one". No marks for a specific fixed number (e.g. "one" or "two") or for talking about constructors without giving a count. P2 is only a small extra for mentioning overloading or differing parameters; do not penalise its absence heavily.
